label: Working together
heading: What we need from you
summary: We do our best work when we can move fast. This is what makes that possible, and what slows it down. We would rather you see it before you sign.

cells: Full access to the website: code, CMS, hosting, and the right to publish
Changes go through your developer or agency as tickets. Each fix waits days.
We edit and ship the same day, several times a week, and test what works.
Tell us before you change the site, the domain or the tracking
A rebuild or domain move happens without us. Pages vanish and tracking breaks.
We plan the change with you, so rankings and tracking survive it.
Data and tool access in week one: Search Console, analytics, tag manager, CRM or revenue data
Access arrives in pieces over months, or sits with IT. We work without knowing what converts.
Everything is granted in the first days. We tie the work to leads and revenue.
One point of contact with the authority to decide
Many people answer, opinions conflict, and questions bounce between them.
One person gathers your team's views and gives us one answer.
Content approved within two working days, or permission to publish and fix after
Every piece waits for several reviewers. Output drops to about one piece a month.
We publish at your package's pace, every week, and results compound.
Legal or compliance review is fine, with a named reviewer, a fixed weekly slot and the rules given up front
Each draft is a new legal question. Writers stop to ask "can we say this?"
We write inside your rules from day one and send one batch a week for review.
Feedback once, in one list, and specific
Feedback arrives in pieces from several people over weeks.
One round of clear notes. We apply them and move on.
Trust the roadmap. Judge us on results, not on daily activity
Daily stand-ups, task-level direction and second-guessing of the plan. The team pulls back, and we end the partnership.
You set the goal, we choose the work. You get a weekly update and a regular call.
Tell us at once when something is wrong
Silence, then a cancellation request.
You flag it the same week. We fix it while it is small.
A realistic clock: about three months before results show
The work is judged in week six and the plan is changed before it can pay off.
A three-month minimum, with leading signs reported along the way.
A stable goal and scope. New asks are priced as new work
The target market or product focus flips mid-way, and extra projects arrive inside the same fee.
The goal is agreed at the start. Changes are discussed and re-scoped.
Your knowledge: brand documents, an hour with your experts, and facts we can verify
We guess at positioning and cannot check claims. Copy stalls or goes out generic.
Content carries what only you know, which is what search and AI answers reward.
Replies within two working days, and attendance at the calls we book
Questions wait weeks. Calls are missed or moved.
Short answers, fast. Blockers clear in a day.
Invoices paid on time
Late payment pauses the work, as the contract says.
Nothing stops.
Respect for the team and their working hours
Night and weekend demands, and criticism without credit.
A team that wants to do its best work for you.

items.text: A reply the same working day.
What shipped, the numbers, and anything we need from you, with a date.
We say so first when we are late or wrong.

update.title: Weekly update
update.note: Every ask comes with a date.

list.headline: Fifteen things,
list.intro: Each row is one thing we ask for. Beside it: what happens without it, and what happens with it.

promise.headline: What you get
promise.intro: The list runs both ways. These are the four things you can hold us to.

message.text: Got it. The fix goes live today, and I will confirm here when it is done.

closing.heading: Want to work this way?
closing.lede: Book a call. We will go through the list together and say plainly what applies to you.
